   "tn14": Over the last five years, has revenue grown every year, operating margin expanded, free cash flow been positive and rising, and cash exceeded debt every year?

summaries.gardner: Fortinet shows several Rule Breaker traits: it leads firewall units (about 55% per 650 Group, Q3 2025), has a founder-CEO (Ken Xie) running it since 2000, and the stock roughly doubled over the past year (+102% to $169.13 on October 16, 2026) while many analysts call it fully valued. It is less of a fit on being a new, disruptive category creator, since firewalls are a maturing market and consumers do not know the brand.
summaries.buffett: Fortinet has a durable cost advantage from its own FortiASIC chips, switching costs on one operating system, very little debt ($496.9 million against $4.47 billion of cash and investments at June 30, 2026) and ten straight years of profits, which suit Buffett's quality tests. The obstacle is price: about 60 times trailing GAAP earnings of $2.83 a share leaves little margin of safety, and the technology is harder to forecast than the businesses Buffett usually owns.
summaries.munger: Munger would like the founder-led, frugal engineering culture and the hard-to-copy chip know-how built since 2000. Inverting, the main ways it could fail are a shift of security to cloud-delivered SASE that shrinks demand for appliances, repeated FortiOS vulnerabilities hurting trust, and a hardware refresh boom fading; at about 60 times earnings the price assumes things go well.
summaries.lynch: Fortinet fits Lynch's fast-grower category, with revenue up from $2,594.4 million in 2020 to $6,799.6 million in 2025 and 2026 guidance of $8.02-8.18 billion, and a simple story of selling firewalls plus recurring subscriptions. But the P/E of about 60 is far above its earnings growth (PEG about 2.9), insiders are selling, and it is a heavily followed stock rather than an overlooked one.
summaries.fisher: Fortinet scores well on Fisher's points: it keeps launching products as firewalls mature (SASE, SecOps, OT and AI data center security), its R&D has produced 1,405 global patents and seven generations of security chips, and it reaches over 500,000 customers through a large channel. Long-tenured founder management and margins that rose from a 20.5% operating margin in 2020 to 30.7% in 2025 also fit, while labour relations and pay are frugal rather than outstanding.
summaries.graham: Fortinet fails most of Graham's defensive-investor tests: it pays no dividend, trades at about 60 times trailing earnings and about 80 times book value, though it is large and has been profitable in each of the last ten years. It is a quality growth stock, not a Graham-style bargain.
summaries.thiel: Fortinet answers several of Thiel's questions well: proprietary ASIC technology that gives better price-performance, a founder-led team, a huge channel distribution engine and a durable position in network security. It is weaker on the 'secret' and on being ten times better, since rivals such as Palo Alto Networks and Cisco compete closely and firewalls are an established category.
summaries.gerstner: Fortinet matches Gerstner's focus on efficient growth: it has passed the 'Rule of 40' easily (about 14% growth plus a 32.7% free-cash-flow margin in 2025) and buys back stock with free cash flow ($2.29 billion in 2025). The stretch is valuation: at about 48 times forward earnings, much of the 2026 product upcycle already looks priced in.
summaries.druckenmiller: Fortinet has the earnings acceleration Druckenmiller looks for: Q2 2026 revenue rose 26% and GAAP EPS 44% to $0.82, billings rose 33%, guidance was raised, and the stock doubled in a year. Risks to the trade are that the firewall refresh cycle is lumpy and the stock already fell 7% on October 16, 2026, ahead of Q3 results due October 28.
summaries.smith: Fortinet fits Terry Smith's 'good company' test well: about 80% gross margins, a GAAP operating margin above 30%, very high returns on capital, little debt and strong cash conversion. Smith's 'don't overpay' rule is the problem, with a free-cash-flow yield of about 2.5% at $169.13.
summaries.greenblatt: Fortinet scores very high on return on capital (about 58% ROIC per StockAnalysis) but poorly on earnings yield, with last-twelve-month operating income of about $2.44 billion against an enterprise value of roughly $121 billion (about 2%). It would not rank near the top of a Magic Formula screen.
summaries.akre: Fortinet fits two legs of Akre's stool: an extraordinary business (high margins, recurring subscriptions, a chip-based cost advantage) and capable, owner-like founder management with a long record. The reinvestment leg is mixed, because most free cash flow goes to buybacks rather than high-return internal reinvestment, and the price is high.
summaries.pabrai: Fortinet is a low-debt, simple-to-explain business, but it does not fit Pabrai's Dhandho approach of buying a temporarily depressed business at a deep discount. At about 60 times earnings after doubling in a year, the 'heads I win, tails I don't lose much' setup is absent.
summaries.wood: Fortinet benefits from AI indirectly, through AI data center security and AI-driven security operations, but it is not one of ARK's core innovation platforms such as AI, robotics, energy storage, blockchain or multiomic sequencing. Its ASIC cost declines do help it, yet it is better seen as a profitable incumbent than a disruptive innovator.
summaries.ackman: Fortinet meets many of Ackman's criteria: a simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generative business with high barriers to entry, little debt and a long-tenured founder. The price, about 60 times trailing earnings, leaves little of the discount to intrinsic value that Pershing Square usually wants.
summaries.sleep: Fortinet partly fits Nick Sleep's 'scale economies shared' idea: it uses its own chips and scale to sell more firewall performance per dollar than rivals, which helped it ship about 55% of firewall units. But it is not obviously sharing savings to the degree Costco or Amazon did, as gross margin stayed around 80% and 2026 prices rose with memory costs.
summaries.valentine: Fortinet solves a large, painful problem, cyberattacks on business networks, in a huge market, as Valentine wants. Founded by Ken and Michael Xie in 2000 after Ken's earlier NetScreen success, it was the kind of technical, market-driven company Sequoia backed, though today it is a mature public company rather than a venture opportunity.
summaries.nash: Fortinet passes much of Nash's quality screen: secular cybersecurity demand, revenue growth above 10%, an operating margin above 30%, far more cash than debt, low short interest (about 2%), consistent earnings beats and a founder-CEO of 25+ years. It fails the valuation steps: Nash's DCF at 12% gives about $67 a share against $169.13, the PEG is about 2.9, and insiders sold about $136 million of stock in the last year with no buying.

momentum.evidence: The shares closed at $169.13 on October 16, 2026, up about 102% over 52 weeks (range $73.55-$197.13) and well above the 200-day average of $123.87, far ahead of the market, despite a 7% drop that day.

g4.evidence: Founder-CEO Ken Xie (NetScreen founder, National Academy of Engineering member) has led Fortinet since 2000 with co-founder Michael Xie as CTO, institutions own about 72% of shares, and it partners with Intel on its SP6 chip and with NVIDIA on BlueField DPUs.

g6.evidence: At about 60 times trailing earnings and 48 times forward, the consensus rating is Hold (44 analysts) with an average target of $167.91, just below the $169.13 price.

simple.evidence: Fortinet sells firewalls and networking hardware (33% of 2025 revenue) plus yearly security subscriptions and support (67%), a business a generalist can understand.

b2.evidence: Revenue rose every year from $1,275.4 million (2016) to $6,799.6 million (2025) and Fortinet was profitable in each of those ten years.

integrity.evidence: Reporting is clear and capital use is disciplined (low debt, buybacks), but Ken Xie is both chairman and CEO, insiders sold about $136 million of stock in the last year, and a 2025 securities class action alleges misleading statements about the firewall refresh cycle.

b6.evidence: Fortinet builds organically around its own FortiOS and FortiASIC rather than doing large acquisitions, with only small tuck-ins in areas such as SASE and data security.

roic.evidence: Return on invested capital is about 58% (StockAnalysis) with a 2025 GAAP operating margin of 30.7%, and debt is only $496.9 million against $4.47 billion of cash and investments.

fcf.evidence: Free cash flow of $2,225.8 million in 2025 (operating cash flow $2,590.6 million minus $364.8 million capex) exceeded net income of $1,853.4 million, helped by upfront subscription billings.

b10.evidence: Retained cash funded growth from $2,594.4 million of revenue (2020) to $6,799.6 million (2025) and buybacks ($2,289.8 million in 2025, $1,500.5 million in 2023) that cut diluted shares from 838.3 million to 764.6 million, with GAAP net income rising from $488.5 million to $1,853.4 million.

safety.evidence: At $169.13 (about 60 times trailing EPS of $2.83), the price is far above a conservative DCF value of about $67 a share.

fairprice.evidence: About 48 times forward earnings and a PEG of about 2.9 is expensive even for 80% gross margins and about 19% guided 2026 revenue growth.

mu5.evidence: With a net cash position, 500,000+ customers and recurring service revenue of $4.58 billion in 2025, failure is unlikely, but cloud SASE substitution, platform consolidation and product vulnerabilities are real ways to lose ground.

reinvest.evidence: Fortinet can reinvest in SASE, SecOps, OT and AI data center security at high returns, but it generates more cash than it can use internally and returns most of it through buybacks.

ly2.evidence: It is a fast grower with a simple story: more firewalls and secure networking gear shipped, followed by recurring subscriptions, with 2026 revenue guided to $8.02-8.18 billion.

ly3.evidence: The trailing P/E of about 60 is far above GAAP EPS growth (diluted EPS up from $2.26 in 2024 to $2.42 in 2025, and up 44% in Q2 2026), giving a PEG of about 2.9.

runway.evidence: Fortinet is expanding from firewalls into SASE (FortiSASE billings grew over 100% in Q2 2026), secure switching and Wi-Fi, OT security and AI data center security, with sales in over 100 countries.

ly7.evidence: The company is shrinking its share count (743 million shares at end-2025 vs 767 million a year earlier; $972.8 million repurchased in H1 2026), but insiders sold about $136 million in the last 12 months with no purchases.

ly8.evidence: Fortinet is a $125 billion company covered by over 40 analysts and owned about 72% by institutions.

fi2.evidence: As branch firewalls mature, Fortinet keeps adding products such as FortiSASE, FortiSIEM/SOAR, OT security and high-speed firewalls for AI data centers, on a seventh-generation security chip (SP6).

fi3.evidence: R&D of $815.5 million in 2025 (12% of revenue) has produced 1,405 global patents and ASICs that give FortiGate leading price-performance and about 55% of firewall unit shipments.

fi4.evidence: Sales and marketing ($2,347.5 million in 2025) drives a large reseller and service-provider channel that reaches over 500,000 customers, and Q2 2026 billings grew 33% to $2,372.1 million.

longterm.evidence: Ken Xie has invested in custom ASICs for over two decades, which he says can take about 10 years to pay back, rather than buying in technology.

gr1.evidence: Fortinet has a market value of about $125 billion and 2025 revenue of $6,799.6 million.

ni10.evidence: GAAP net income was positive in each year from 2016 ($32.2 million) to 2025 ($1,853.4 million).

gr4.evidence: Fortinet pays no dividend; it returns cash through share buybacks.

eps10.evidence: Diluted EPS rose from $0.18 in 2016 (about $0.04 after the 2022 five-for-one split) to $2.42 in 2025.

gr6.evidence: At $169.13 the stock trades at about 60 times trailing EPS of $2.83, far above 15 times average earnings.

gr7.evidence: P/E of about 60 times a price-to-book of about 80 (equity of $1,551.1 million at June 30, 2026) is far above 22.5.

th1.evidence: FortiASIC gives Fortinet a large price-performance advantage over CPU-based firewalls, but not a tenfold edge in overall security quality over Palo Alto Networks or Check Point.

timing.evidence: A firewall refresh cycle, AI data center build-outs and SASE adoption lifted Q2 2026 product revenue 52% and billings 33%.

th3.evidence: Fortinet started with unified threat management for small and mid-size businesses and has expanded into enterprise firewalls, SD-WAN, switching, Wi-Fi, SASE and security operations.

team.evidence: Ken Xie co-founded Fortinet with his brother Michael in 2000 after founding NetScreen (sold to Juniper for $4 billion), and has led it for over 25 years.

th5.evidence: Fortinet sells mainly through a large network of resellers, distributors and service providers in over 100 countries, reaching over 500,000 customers.

durable.evidence: Switching costs on FortiOS and its chip cost edge are durable, but cloud-delivered security (Zscaler, Netskope) and platform consolidation by Palo Alto, Cisco and Microsoft could erode the appliance-centred franchise over 10-20 years.

th7.evidence: Fortinet's bet on custom security chips and converging networking with security was distinctive, but these ideas are now widely understood and partly copied.

trend.evidence: It benefits from rising cyberattacks and AI data center security, but it is not a leading AI or cloud platform beneficiary in the way cloud-native security vendors are.

dr1.evidence: Growth is accelerating: Q2 2026 GAAP EPS rose 44% to $0.82 versus 7% diluted EPS growth for all of 2025 ($2.42 vs $2.26), and 2026 guidance was raised to $8.02-8.18 billion of revenue and $3.41-3.47 of non-GAAP EPS.

dr2.evidence: Strong billings ($2,372.1 million in Q2 2026, +33%) and deferred revenue of $7,675.7 million support growth, but the product surge may be a refresh-cycle peak that slows in 2027.

dr4.evidence: With net cash and little interest exposure, rates matter little, but customer IT budgets and memory/component cost inflation (which forced 2026 price increases) are macro-sensitive.

dr6.evidence: Q3 2026 results on October 28, 2026, the ongoing firewall refresh cycle and FortiSASE growth are identifiable catalysts.

dr7.evidence: After a doubling and with the stock near the average analyst target, the risk/reward does not clearly justify a large concentrated position.

gm.evidence: GAAP gross margin was 80.5% in 2025 and 80.2% in Q2 2026.

fcfyield.evidence: Last-twelve-month free cash flow of about $3.1 billion against a market value of about $125 billion is a yield of about 2.5%, low for roughly 20% growth.

gb2.evidence: Last-twelve-month operating income of about $2.44 billion is only about 2% of an enterprise value of roughly $121 billion.

pa2.evidence: Fortinet is not in a setback: Q2 2026 revenue rose 26% and guidance was raised; the 2024-2025 firewall slowdown has already reversed.

pa4.evidence: The business has net cash and recurring revenue, so permanent business impairment is unlikely, but at about 60 times earnings a derating could cause lasting losses for buyers at today's price.

wo1.evidence: Fortinet is a cybersecurity and networking vendor that uses AI in its products, not a leader in AI, robotics, energy storage, blockchain or multiomic sequencing.

wo2.evidence: Each FortiASIC generation lowers cost per unit of firewall throughput, but 2026 memory cost increases pushed prices up rather than opening big new demand through falling costs.

wo3.evidence: Fortinet relies mainly on security and networking, with AI as a feature rather than a combination of several innovation platforms.

wo4.evidence: Its markets (firewall, SD-WAN, SASE, secure networking) are growing, but not plausibly many times larger within five years.

ac3.evidence: With net cash, interest rates hardly matter, but memory and component prices affect hardware costs, as seen in its 2026 cost-linked price increases.

ns1.evidence: Its ASICs let it offer more performance per dollar than rivals and win unit share, but gross margin has held around 80% rather than being passed on, and 2026 prices rose.

ns4.evidence: Expansion into SASE and secure networking could strengthen it, but cloud-native rivals and platform consolidators make its 10-20 year position uncertain.

va2.evidence: Cyberattacks and ransomware are a large, costly problem for businesses, governments and hospitals, which Fortinet's firewalls and services address.

tn1.evidence: Cybersecurity is a real secular trend and Fortinet sells infrastructure-layer security, but it was built for network security before AI, not specifically for the AI trend.

tn2.evidence: The market often sees Fortinet as a cyclical firewall hardware vendor, while services are 67% of revenue and it is pushing into SASE and AI data center security, though this gap is fairly well understood.

tn3.evidence: It is a $125 billion U.S. company founded in 2000, not a small cap, Chinese company, commodity producer, airline, seasonal business or startup.

tn4.evidence: Revenue grew every year from 2020 to 2025, 2025 net income was $1,853.4 million, and cash and investments ($4.47 billion) far exceed debt ($496.9 million).

tn21.evidence: There is no co-CEO, acquisition spree, accounting issue or auditor change and margins are rising, but insiders (Ken Xie, Michael Xie, COO John Whittle) sold about $136 million of stock in the last year as it doubled.

tn22.evidence: Fortinet has $6.8 billion of revenue, strong profits and shrinks its share count through buybacks rather than selling shares.

tn24.evidence: At $169.13, a DCF at 12% needs revenue growth and margins far above the roughly 15% three-year average growth and 32% free-cash-flow margin it is delivering.

tn25.evidence: Nash's DCF (15.5% three-year average growth, 32.3% FCF margin, 12% discount, 4% terminal, plus about $3.97 billion net cash) gives about $67 a share, well below $169.13.

tn26.evidence: It easily passes the Rule of 40, but at about 48 times forward earnings the PEG is about 2.9, well above 1.
